chapter: After the Army: school, race, politics
title: Chronology: job, draft, Cannonball, the band, then Wayne State
summary: Brower clarifies the sequence from the factory job to being drafted at 19, Cannonball, the Army band, and Wayne State.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I just want to get the chronology straight. You were able to manipulate your records to get a job, knowing that if you went into the Army, you could come back.
I didn’t know I was going to go into the Army. I was sucked up! “You’re 19! How did you miss this! They started drafting at 18! Get in that service”
So you got the job, and then you were sucked into the service.

Okay, now tomorrow we are going to have to come and fill in the blanks of how you developed as a musician in Detroit. We haven’t talked about that. Just to, sort of, understand this chronology: you get the job, you get into the service, you meet Cannonball in the service, you go through that, then you integrate this band, then you come—when you muster out, Cannonball tries to get you to FAMU. It doesn’t work, and you end up at Wayne State.
